content: 1. The administration of rolapitant can increase the plasma levels or effects of citalopram by inhibiting the hepatic enzyme CYP2D6 metabolism. It is recommended to use caution and monitor the patient closely. 2. Rolapitant may elevate plasma concentrations of CYP2D6 substrates for at least 28 days following its administration. This necessitates careful monitoring when co-administering drugs metabolized by CYP2D6. 3. Rolapitant increases the levels or effects of clomipramine by affecting CYP2D6 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 4. Rolapitant can enhance the plasma concentrations of clonidine by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor the patient. 5. Oral rolapitant, as a P-glycoprotein (P-gp) inhibitor, may increase plasma concentrations of P-gp substrates, potentially leading to adverse reactions. Monitor for adverse effects if co-administration with P-gp substrates cannot be avoided. 6. Rolapitant increases the levels or effects of codeine by inhibiting CYP2D6 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 7. Rolapitant can elevate plasma concentrations of cyclosporine by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor the patient. 8. Rolapitant increases the levels or effects of desipramine by inhibiting CYP2D6 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 9. Rolapitant enhances the levels or effects of deutetrabenazine by inhibiting CYP2D6 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. Strong CYP2D6 inhibitors can increase systemic exposure to active dihydro-metabolites of deutetrabenazine by approximately threefold. Do not exceed 18 mg per dose and 36 mg per day of deutetrabenazine when co-administered with strong CYP2D6 inhibitors. 10. Rolapitant increases the levels or effects of dextroamphetamine transdermal by inhibiting CYP2D6 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are advised. Initiate with lower doses and monitor for serotonin syndrome, especially during initiation or dosage increases. Discontinue dextroamphetamine transdermal and CYP2D6 inhibitors if serotonin syndrome occurs. 11. Rolapitant elevates the levels or effects of dextromethorphan by inhibiting CYP2D6 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are necessary. Monitor for adverse reactions when co-administration with narrow therapeutic index CYP2D6 substrates is unavoidable. 12. Rolapitant increases the levels or effects of digoxin by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor digoxin concentrations with concomitant rolapitant use, adjusting the dosage if necessary. 13. Rolapitant enhances the levels or effects of doxepin by inhibiting CYP2D6 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 14. Rolapitant increases the levels or effects of doxorubicin by inhibiting CYP2D6 metabolism. Use caution and monitor the patient. 15. Rolapitant elevates the levels or effects of duloxetine by inhibiting CYP2D6 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 16. Rolapitant increases the levels or effects of duvelisib by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter and other mechanisms. Use caution and monitor the patient. Co-administration of duvelisib (a BCRP substrate) with a BCRP transport inhibitor may increase duvelisib levels or effects. 17. Elagolix decreases the levels of rolapitant by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. Elagolix is a weak-to-moderate CYP3A4 inducer. Monitor CYP3A substrates if co-administered and consider increasing the CYP3A substrate dose if needed. 18. Rolapitant increases the levels or effects of eliglustat by inhibiting CYP2D6 metabolism. Use caution and monitor the patient. 19. Encorafenib affects rolapitant by inhibiting and inducing CYP3A4 metabolism at clinically relevant plasma concentrations. Use caution and monitor the patient. Co-administration with sensitive CYP3A4 substrates may increase toxicity or reduce efficacy of these agents. 20. Fedratinib increases the levels or effects of rolapitant by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and adjust the dose of CYP3A4 substrates as necessary. 21. Rolapitant elevates the levels or effects of flecainide by inhibiting CYP2D6 metabolism. Use caution and monitor the patient. 22. Rolapitant increases the levels or effects of fluoxetine by inhibiting CYP2D6 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 23. Rolapitant enhances the levels or effects of fluphenazine by inhibiting CYP2D6 metabolism. Use caution and monitor the patient. 24. Rolapitant increases the levels or effects of fluvoxamine by inhibiting CYP2D6 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 25. Rolapitant elevates the levels or effects of glecaprevir/pibrentasvir by decreasing metabolism. Use caution and monitor the patient. Exercise caution when co-administering glecaprevir/pibrentasvir with P-gp/BCRP inhibitors. 26. Rolapitant increases the levels or effects of haloperidol by inhibiting CYP2D6 metabolism. Use caution and monitor the patient. 27. Rolapitant enhances the levels or effects of iloperidone by inhibiting CYP2D6 metabolism. Use caution and monitor the patient. 28. Rolapitant increases the levels or effects of imipramine by inhibiting CYP2D6 metabolism. Use caution and monitor the patient. 29. Rolapitant elevates the levels or effects of irinotecan by inhibiting BCRP transport. Use caution and monitor for adverse reactions if co-administration with BCRP substrates cannot be avoided. 30. Istradefylline increases the levels or effects of rolapitant by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor the patient. Istradefylline 40 mg/day increased peak levels and AUC of CYP3A4 substrates in clinical trials. This effect was not observed with istradefylline 20 mg/day. Consider dose reduction of sensitive CYP3A4 substrates. 31. Rolapitant increases the levels or effects of lofexidine by inhibiting CYP2D6 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. Concomitant use with strong CYP2D6 inhibitors may increase lofexidine plasma levels. Monitor for symptoms of orthostasis and bradycardia, and consider dose reduction of lofexidine. 32. Lorlatinib decreases the levels or effects of rolapitant by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor the patient. 33. Rolapitant enhances the levels or effects of maprotiline by inhibiting CYP2D6 metabolism. Use caution and monitor the patient. 34. Rolapitant increases the levels or effects of mavorixafor by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Therapy modification and close monitoring are necessary. Monitor mavorixafor if co-administered with P-gp inhibitors and reduce the dose if needed. 35. Rolapitant elevates the levels or effects of methamphetamine by inhibiting CYP2D6 metabolism. Use caution and monitor the patient. 36. Rolapitant increases the levels or effects of methotrexate by inhibiting BCRP transport. Use caution and monitor for adverse reactions if co-administration with BCRP substrates cannot be avoided. 37. Rolapitant enhances the levels or effects of metoprolol by inhibiting CYP2D6 metabolism. Use caution and monitor the patient. 38. Rolapitant increases the levels or effects of mirtazapine by inhibiting CYP2D6 metabolism. Use caution and monitor the patient. 39. Rolapitant elevates the levels or effects of nebivolol by inhibiting CYP2D6 metabolism. Use caution and monitor the patient. 40. Rolapitant increases the levels or effects of oliceridine by inhibiting CYP2D6 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. If concomitant use is necessary, less frequent oliceridine dosing may be required. Monitor closely for respiratory depression and sedation, and titrate subsequent doses accordingly. If the inhibitor is discontinued, consider increasing the oliceridine dosage until stable drug effects are achieved. Monitor for signs of opioid withdrawal. 41. Rolapitant enhances the levels or effects of paroxetine by inhibiting CYP2D6 metabolism. Use caution and monitor the patient. 42. Rolapitant increases the levels or effects of perphenazine by inhibiting CYP2D6 metabolism. Use caution and monitor the patient. 43. Rolapitant elevates the levels or effects of pitolisant by inhibiting CYP2D6 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are necessary. For patients currently taking pitolisant, reduce the pitolisant dose by half upon initiating strong CYP2D6 inhibitors. 44. Rolapitant increases the levels or effects of promethazine by inhibiting CYP2D6 metabolism. Use caution and monitor the patient. 45. Rolapitant enhances the levels or effects of propafenone by inhibiting CYP2D6 metabolism. Use caution and monitor the patient. 46. Rolapitant increases the levels or effects of propranolol by inhibiting CYP2D6 metabolism. Use caution and monitor the patient. 47. Rolapitant elevates the levels or effects of protriptyline by inhibiting CYP2D6 metabolism. Use caution and monitor the patient. 48. Rolapitant increases the levels or effects of risperidone by inhibiting CYP2D6 metabolism. Use caution and monitor the patient. 49. Rolapitant enhances the levels or effects of ritonavir by inhibiting CYP2D6 metabolism. Use caution and monitor the patient. 50. Rolapitant increases the levels or effects of rosuvastatin by inhibiting BCRP transport. Use caution and monitor for adverse reactions when co-administration with narrow therapeutic index BCRP substrates is unavoidable. Use the lowest effective dose of rosuvastatin. 51. Rucaparib increases the levels or effects of rolapitant by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. Adjust the dosage of CYP3A4 substrates if clinically indicated. 52. Rolapitant elevates the levels of seladelpar by inhibiting BCRP transport. Use caution and monitor for adverse effects if co-administered with BCRP inhibitors. 53. Rolapitant increases the levels or effects of selexipag by inhibiting BCRP transport. Use caution and monitor the patient.
